en.title: Number of Distinct Palindromic Substrings
en.description:
Count the palindromic substrings with distinct text; multiple occurrences count only once. The correct answer for the long original OCR example abcddcbabcdcdaadcdcbabcddcb is 26, not 27; the original enumeration contains duplicates and substrings that do not exist.

The input/output protocol was compiled by this site; missing numeric bounds and recoveries of source typos are all stated explicitly.
en.input: One line containing a lowercase string; complete OCR range 1≤length≤5000.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The outputs of the three public examples are, in order: 7; 5; 26. These answers were verified by independent enumeration or direct simulation.
hints: Build a palindromic tree with two special roots of lengths −1 and 0; for each added character, follow the failure links from the longest palindromic suffix to find a node that can be extended, then create the new palindrome and its failure link.
